key_insight: Real patient-chatbot conversations are far more diverse than idealized simulations, and that diversity can change AI triage outcomes.
clinical_relevance: Conversational health AI should be designed and tested to handle varied communication styles and emotions to avoid unsafe or inequitable urgency assessments.
method: Built a patient simulator modeling clinical content, emotion, strategy, and communication style
Tested 4 LLMs across 1,164 clinician-graded cases using 5 patient personae
evidence_signal: In a Turing-inspired realism test with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with graders identifying them correctly only 55% of the time.
watch_item: Results may not generalize if deployed systems are evaluated only on cooperative, well-structured patients, because real-world communication diversity can shift triage decisions.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
